searchText: For the CL it will always land on `==`, but since slots can be empty sometimes the fork will happen on `>` for the EL. By having the fork timestamp be an odd number, it ensures that it always triggers on `>` for both clients (fewer codepaths/confusion when the fork slot is missing a block). But then it can’t be specified as an epoch which makes life much more complex. Better to just have >=. It’s easy to cover with a single test CL call in 9 minutes https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/629 https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/91725886939?pwd=b2kzT0JGeFAzTmhyb1BYSTgrZ0xwdz09
